14.0.s.en: 1. The ship or the wooden idol?

14.0.0.en: 1 And another, before he sails on the sea and goes upon the raging waves, calls upon a piece of wood more fragile than the vessel that carries him. 2 For the vessel was devised by the desire for gain, and the wisdom of the craftsman built it; 3 but Your providence, O Father, is that which governs it, for You have made a way in the sea, and a safe path in the waves, 4 showing that You can save from every danger, even if a man should go to sea without skill. 5 And You love that the works of Your wisdom should not be in vain; therefore men entrust their lives to a very small piece of wood, and pass over the deep in a ship and are saved. 6 For in the beginning also, when the proud giants perished, the hope of the world fled to a ship, and Your hand guided it, and left to all ages a seed of generations. 7 For blessed is the wood by which righteousness comes; 8 but the wood that is made an idol is cursed, both it and he that made it: he, because he made it; and it, because, being corruptible, it was called god. 9 For the ungodly and his ungodliness are alike hateful to God, 10 and the thing made shall be punished with him that made it. 11 Therefore there shall be a visitation also upon the idols of the Gentiles, because in the creation of God they have become an abomination, and a stumbling block to the souls of men, and a snare to the feet of the foolish. Here the wise man speaks of those who are skillful in building ships, and then fix a wooden image of the god at the prow or the stern of the ship, supposing that it is able to protect the ship, and offering it daily sacrifices.

14.0.1.en: The Book of Acts (Acts 28:11) refers to such a matter, where it mentions an Alexandrian ship marked with the sign of Gemini or the Twin Brothers, who were regarded as the sons of the Greek god Zeus, Castor and Pollux. The sailors used to set their image on their ships as two gods who preserve ships from sinking.

14.0.2.en: God gave man the skill to build ships with wisdom, as He gave this skill to those who made the tabernacle of meeting (Ex 31:3; 35:31, 35; Wis 8:6). But it is God who preserves the ship, for the wisdom of God is what leads the world on land and sea and in the air and space.

14.0.3.en: And another, before he sails on the sea and goes upon the raging waves, calls upon a piece of wood more fragile than the vessel that carries him. [1]

14.0.4.en: He gives the example of the sailor who calls upon a wooden god whose material is worse than the wood from which his ship was made. Thus the author mocks the idol itself, as well as the one who takes refuge in it.

14.0.5.en: What folly, that man should resort for help in the midst of the sea to the wood of an idol, instead of trusting in the wood of the ship, which is built and steered with wisdom from above...

14.0.6.en: How can the weak protect one who is stronger than he? These wooden gods are far weaker than the ship, and therefore weaker than the man who made the ship.

14.1.0.en: For the desire of gain devised this vessel, and the artisan wisdom built it. [2]

14.1.1.en: The wise man compares the maker of the ship with the maker of the wooden idol. Both the ship and the wooden idol are the work of man and reveal his skill. But the first offered what is for the benefit of mankind, since there is need of sailing, whether for fishing or for travel between the coastal countries, while the second spoils his time with what corrupts the minds of the simple.

14.1.2.en: It is fitting for the makers of idols not to waste their gifts and skill and abilities on defective idols that are of no use, but to use them for what edifies mankind, such as shipbuilding, and so on.

14.2.0.en: But Your providence, O Father, is what guides it, for You have made a way even in the sea, and in the waves a safe path. [3]

14.2.1.en: Here he calls the divine wisdom “divine providence,” for the wisdom of God is infinite love. For the first time the expression “divine providence” appears in the Bible, though it is an idea that the Bible affirms in both the Old and New Testaments (Josh 4:24; 1 Kgs 18:46).

14.2.2.en: Divine providence means the divine love ever working on behalf of the creation beloved by God, and it is a creative work.

14.2.3.en: God's surpassing providence appeared when He set up a way for His people and believers, and a safe path in the waves, which Noah and his family experienced in the midst of the Flood, and the people of Israel during their Exodus and their crossing of the Red Sea into the wilderness.

14.2.4.en: In the midst of the waves of the sea of this world the believer leans on the breast of God, the Creator of land and sea, and is at peace, sheltered under the wings of divine providence.

14.2.5.en: Jonah the prophet found no way sweeter and safer than that which God gave him when the sailors cast him into the raging sea. The Lord had prepared a great fish to swallow him (Jon 1:17). Inside it he enjoyed a unique ship not made by man; he lifted his heart to God and enjoyed what the high priests did not enjoy in the Holy of Holies, for he says: “My prayer came in unto You, into Your holy temple” (Jon 2:7). He offered a unique hymn of the joy of the resurrection: “Salvation is of the Lord” (Jon 2:9). St. Jacob of Serugh sees him as a deposit kept in the belly of the fish. Where there is no hope, hope in the Lord was revealed before him, and where death was found, it touched the new, risen life!

14.2.6.en: * Then the Lord prepared a fish, as it is written, and it swallowed Jonah to magnify him amid the waves. A great fish received him in amazement, and kept him as a deposit so that the waves surrounding him might not buffet him.

14.2.7.en: In the place where he had no hope, hope met him, and from within death life sprang forth by a hidden symbol.

14.2.8.en: In the place where there was no covering and no savior, tenderness covered him, that he might recover life from death.

14.2.9.en: * Jonah went on the fearful road without a companion. And mercies followed him and became his companions...

14.2.10.en: He hurried on his way to a terrifying place without fear. And where there are no saviors or keepers, the Lord kept the son of the Hebrews that he might not be corrupted...

14.2.11.en: A new ship Jonah acquired that was not broken, and he sat and went swiftly in the heart of the sea.

14.2.12.en: A marvelous ship that dives and probes the depths of the sea, and its cargo is kept, no harm reaching it.

14.2.13.en: A ship moving not by the winds on the face of the waters but by the heat within the waters without sailors.

14.2.14.en: He dwelt in a house that moves among the waves in amazement, and when it turns over it does not empty what is in it.

14.2.15.en: * His speech is marvelous, a priest praying at length, and his temple among the waves in haste.

14.2.16.en: The altar inside the fish, and the voice instead of offerings, and the Holy of Holies which none enters but one (the high priest).

14.2.17.en: A temple built by none but One who was born within the waters. The priest came from the dry land and entered and sanctified in it.

14.2.18.en: In the tabernacle there is Aaron, and on the top of the mountain Elijah, and in the temple Solomon, and inside the fish Jonah. It is a virgin altar in which no one has entered to serve as priest since the priest, radiant in his unique service, entered it.

14.2.19.en: A marvelous speech, when (Jonah) thundered in the belly of the fish, and his prayer went up, and there was nothing to hinder it.

14.2.20.en: His prayer cleft the depths, and the seas did not hinder it; it flew to the heights, and the great deep did not drown it.

14.2.21.en: It pressed on and entered among the angels and was not prevented. The ranks of the fiery ones met it and it was not rebuked.

14.2.22.en: (The prayer) bound its hands, and cried out in pain before the divine majesty. It bowed its head and asked mercy of the divine tenderness. It was troubled, and its voice thundered with supplication upon its sweet harp, and its mouth spoke asking for mercies. “My Lord, that servant imprisoned at the bottom of the sea sent me, and I have come to present the petition.”

14.3.0.en: St. Jacob of Serugh Showing that You can save from every danger, even if a man should go to sea without skill. [4]

14.3.1.en: Jonah had no skill to steer a fish in the sea, being in its belly, but he realized that the true Pilot is He who prepared the fish for him.

14.3.2.en: He saved him from danger, and even brought him into surpassing glories. And God saved His people of old, who lived in Egypt tending cattle and had no experience of the seas, so that they walked on dry ground in the midst of the waters, where no human feet had passed before and none passed after in this surpassing manner. How great is God's care and His love for us, even when we have no skill in crossing dangerous ways!

14.4.0.en: You love that the works of Your wisdom should not be barren, and therefore men entrust their lives to a small piece of wood, and cross the waves on a raft and are saved. [5]

14.4.1.en: It is out of God's love for us that He uses small things for our salvation, that we may feel His providence and not rely on our abilities, as though we were able to save ourselves by our own human efforts. Often large ships become a place of danger for those on them, and the travelers, like the sailors, resort to simple pieces of wood that cannot be compared with the greatness of the ship, and those who escape the danger feel that they were carried not on pieces of wood but on the divine arms. In the midst of the dangerous waves the Apostle Paul says: “we let her drive” (Acts 27:15).

14.5.0.en: And in the beginning, when the proud giants were perishing, the hope of the world took refuge on a raft, and Your hand guided it, and left to all ages a seed of generations. [6]

14.5.1.en: The wise man often refers to the story of the Flood, in which wicked men supposed in their pride that there was none who could restrain them from their evils, and they perished in the Flood. But Noah and his family, that is, the company of believers, entered the wooden ark as though it were a lifebuoy, and passed through the destructive period of the Flood, to go out into a world renewed for their service. God preserved these eight souls for the renewal of mankind.

14.5.2.en: * When the work of the builders went on and drew near its end, the wicked laughed at the venerable man and mocked him. He was telling them what he heard from God, and they multiplied insults to his teaching. My brethren, perhaps they thought him mad, since he multiplied his warnings, and they threw mockery at his ark. He sighed over the wicked because they were ignorant, and they laughed at the work that he was carrying out. He began to build the new chamber from planks set in order according to measures he took from God; the building rose and was finished after a hundred years, and then all the work was completed (Gen 5:32; 6:8, 11). The voice of Noah the righteous became hoarse as he preached, and the sons of iniquity neglected and sinned the more. He offered them teaching as far as he could, and the iniquity of the earth was multiplying more and more. His great work bore witness to his words, and no comic tale was being told by the righteous man; that marvelous perfection which he made showed the truth he spoke. It was necessary for the wicked generation to know that Noah was not laboring in vain in his work. Their eyes despised the great sight, and their ears despised the preaching; they did not understand by the work that was done there, nor were they guided by the voice of teaching. Their hearts and their eyes with their ears were closed, because the doors of their thoughts were shut by their own will. When the measure of the sins of the wicked overflowed, and the opportunity of repentance was lessened and diminished, when the whole generation was corrupted by cutting off hope and by wrath, He shut the door of mercies and confined them. When the Avenger waited and tarried that they might ask of Him, and no voice was found pleading to obtain forgiveness, then grace was ashamed before justice: How long will You be longsuffering, since they have gained no benefit?

14.5.3.en: When the stories of that ark were built, nothing remained but that Noah should enter, and then wrath would come.

14.6.0.en: St. Jacob of Serugh For blessed is the wood by which righteousness comes. [7]

14.6.1.en: God used the wood of the ark to rescue His believers, instead of the wooden idols that sailors suppose able to rescue them from the dangers of the seas, whether the raging waves or the pirates of the seas.

14.6.2.en: Here he compares the wooden idol with the wood of the Cross. The first is an idol that falls under the curse, with its maker and the one who worships it. But the second bore the Savior of the whole world.

14.6.3.en: * The Lord of Abraham came to the house of His friends to visit them, and when the sons of Abraham went out they gave Him the Cross. He was carrying His Cross, and going out from the one who crucified Him, her Lord, because she gave Him in return for His kindnesses nothing but this (the Cross). He became a physician to her and healed all her wounds, and when He went out He took no provision but the Cross. The sentence of iniquity was passed on the Son of God, and He went out to die with the wicked without guilt (Mk 15:28).

14.6.4.en: St. Jacob of Serugh * The Gospel says: “And they took Jesus, and led Him away. And He bearing His cross went forth into a place called the place of a skull” (Jn 19:16-17).

14.6.5.en: Jesus went forth to the place where He was to be crucified, bearing His Cross...

14.6.7.en: The wicked beholder sees it as a sight full of mockery, but the godly beholder sees it as a great mystery!

14.6.8.en: The wicked sees in it a great confirmation of disgrace and shame, and the godly sees it as an impregnable fortress of faith!

14.6.9.en: The wicked sees it and laughs, seeing a King carrying the tree of punishment instead of the scepter of kingship, but the godly sees a King carrying the Cross for his own crucifixion... where the Cross will be set upon the foreheads... as the Apostle Paul says: “But God forbid that I should glory, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ” (Gal 6:14).

14.6.10.en: He was praising the very Cross of Christ, which He bore upon His shoulders, as a shining lamp burning without being put under a bushel (Mt 5:15).

14.6.11.en: St. Augustine * By the tree by which (Satan) killed us, the Lord rescued us!

14.6.12.en: By the wine by which we became crazed, we became (in Communion) pure!

14.6.13.en: From the (divine) side a secret power flowed, which shattered Satan like Dagon (1 Sam 5:1-5), for in this ark is hidden a book that cries out for us: “The Conqueror” (the Lord Christ)!

14.6.14.en: Blessed is He who as a true Lamb saved us, and destroyed our destroyer as happened with Dagon!

14.6.15.en: The old wolf (Satan) saw the Lamb... and was terrified of Him though he hid himself. For as the wolf put on the garment of lambs, so the Shepherd became a “Lamb” among the lambs, so that when the greedy wolf dared to devour the gentle Lamb, this Almighty One would repel that devourer!

14.7.0.en: St. Ephrem the Syrian But that which is made an idol is cursed, both it and he that made it: he, because he made it; and it, because, being corruptible, it was called god. [8]

14.7.1.en: The wise man offers the mystery of the curse of both the material of the idol and its maker. The material in itself is not evil, nor is man as God's creature evil, for all that God created is good. The evil of the material lies in its use as an idol, which usurps the glory of God and which the devil inhabits to deceive men by it. And the evil of man is not in his body nor in his soul, but in the perversion of his will, in which he bears a will that resists the divine truth.

14.7.2.en: The world is beautiful and good, and the body is good and the soul is good; the deviation of any creature from the course for which it was created corrupts its being and makes it evil.

14.7.3.en: * “But that which is made an idol is cursed, both it and he that made it” (Wis 14:8) does not mean that what has no life in it is cursed in itself, but by the word “made” he means precisely the lifeless idol (in which Satan dwells).

14.8.0.en: Origen For God hates the ungodly and his ungodliness alike. [9]

14.8.1.en: God does not hate His creation, but He cannot bear what is not in harmony with His holiness. The wicked man who denies the faith, whether by his mouth or by his work, cannot enjoy fellowship with the Holy One unless he accepts sanctification by the Spirit of God.

14.8.2.en: Here God hates the evil will of the wicked man, as He hates evil itself.

14.9.0.en: So the thing made and the maker are punished. [10]

14.9.1.en: Often God allowed the prophets to destroy idols, as Moses the prophet did, who ground the golden calf to powder and scattered it (Ex 32:20). As for idolaters, God allows them to be disciplined in this world, and if they do not cease, their punishment will be the eternal fire of Gehenna.

14.10.0.en: Therefore there shall be a visitation also upon the idols of the Gentiles, because they have become an abomination in God's creation, and a stumbling block to the souls of men, and a snare to the feet of the foolish. [11]

14.10.1.en: Sadly, Solomon the wise himself, when he married foreign pagan women, worshipped their gods (1 Kgs 11:8); how much more are simple souls exposed to fall into this worship!

14.11.0.en: 12 For the devising of idols was the beginning of fornication, and the invention of them the corruption of life. 13 For they were not from the beginning, neither shall they be for ever. The idea of making idols is the origin of fornication, and the invention of them is the corruption of life. [12]

14.11.1.en: Man was created bearing within himself a natural law that urges him to worship the living God, and he finds rest and peace in fulfilling this impulse; but when man turned his back to God and rejected His divine commandment, the lusts of his body rose against him and took possession of and ruled over his will. At the same time he wants to worship, so he exchanged the invisible God, who rebukes his conscience, for false gods that he sees and touches and appeases by every means, even by wounding his body or slaughtering his children, to quiet his conscience.

14.11.2.en: Idol worship is bound up with fornication. For on one side the relation of believers with God is like the relation of a bride with her bridegroom, so that if she turns her back to Him to be joined to pagan gods she has fallen into marital unfaithfulness. Therefore it was said of unfaithful Israel: “Where is the bill of your mother's divorcement?” (Isa 50:1). It was also said: “Take heed to yourself, lest you make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land, and they go a whoring after their gods, and do sacrifice unto their gods, and one call you, and you eat of his sacrifice; and you take of their daughters unto your sons, and their daughters go a whoring after their gods, and make your sons go a whoring after their gods” (Ex 34:15-16). The origin of idolatry is the corruption of man's thought and unfaithfulness to God the Creator, which is counted as fornication of the soul that abandons its union with its Creator to be joined to accursed idols.

14.11.3.en: On the other hand, idolatry has often been bound up with bodily fornication, sometimes even in the temples of the idols themselves.

14.11.4.en: The connection of idolatry with fornication appears from what is recorded of the people's worship of the golden calf, for it was said: “the people sat down to eat and to drink, and rose up to play” (Ex 32:6). Here “play” means sexual caresses.

14.11.5.en: * (Idol worship) was discovered among men for no reason other than the existence of passions among those who imagined it.

14.11.6.en: * When the human soul had experienced various pleasures, and forgot divine things, and was the more delighted with the pleasures of the body that it set before its eyes, and cared for nothing but present things and contemplating them, it no longer thought that there is any good except temporal and bodily things. Therefore, having turned aside and forgotten that it was in the image of the good God, it no longer had the power by which it saw God the Word, after whose likeness it was created. But having withdrawn from itself, it began to imagine and fancy what has no existence.

14.11.7.en: * When the men of the former age lost their minds, and sank in passions and the fancies of bodily things, and forgot the knowledge of God and His glory because of the dullness of their minds, or rather the absence of their minds, they made for themselves gods of visible things, glorifying the creature rather than the Creator God, and deifying the things made rather than the Lord, their cause and Creator.

14.11.8.en: Pope Athanasius the Apostolic * He who serves vain gods is without doubt an adulterer away from the truth, for all vanity is fornication. Thus he sinks into fornication.

14.11.9.en: Tertullian * Blessed is Rachel, who hid the idols of the vain Gentiles and declared that their images were full of uncleanness. And let no one think that she offended against the honor of her father and her reverence for him as a father, because she sat while he stood (Gen 31:35). For it is written: “He that loves father or mother more than Me is not worthy of Me” (Mt 10:37).

14.11.10.en: The woman who commits adultery does not cleave to her husband, and is not one flesh with him (1 Cor 6:15-16), but isolates herself and separates herself from him by her adultery. So every soul that does not cleave to God but walks in fornication by submitting to the worship of vain idols is separated from the Lord by the grievous defilement of holy things, when it ought to have cleaved to Him. And he who withdraws from the Lord perishes.

14.12.0.en: They were not in the beginning, neither shall they be for ever. [13]

14.12.1.en: When man was created good and pure, purity was bound up with the worship of God the Creator from the beginning. But when corruption gained mastery over man, and he enslaved himself to bodily pleasures and fell into fornication, he turned aside from worshipping the Holy One and began to worship idols or creatures, and these will pass away one day.

14.12.2.en: Cleaving to the true, holy God brings us into immortality, where divine righteousness is, while indulgence in bodily lusts drives us to perdition and destruction, because they do not last.

14.13.0.en: 14 For by the vain glory of men they entered into the world, and therefore shall they come shortly to an end.

14.13.1.en: They entered the world through men's love of vainglory, and therefore a speedy end was written for them. [14]

14.13.2.en: Besides fornication there is another motive for idol worship, namely the love of vainglory. For the worship of the humble God moves the soul to enjoy inner glory, but the worship of vain idols glorifies man and his handiwork.

14.13.3.en: It is as though the worship of the humble Holy One is bound up with humble souls, and the worship of idols and enslavement to the proud Satan is bound up with man's fall. We do not wonder at the warning of Holy Scripture: “God resists the proud.”

14.14.0.en: 15 For a father afflicted with untimely mourning, when he has made an image of his child who was suddenly taken away, now honored him as a god, who was then a dead man, and delivered to those that were under him ceremonies and sacrifices. 16 Thus in process of time an ungodly custom, grown strong, was kept as a law, and graven images were worshipped by the commandments of kings. 17 Whom men could not honor in presence, because they dwelt far off, they took the counterfeit of his visage from afar, and made an express image of a king whom they honored, to flatter the absent as if he were present.

14.14.1.en: There is a father afflicted with untimely mourning, who made an image of his son who was suddenly taken away, and began to honor with the honor of a god him who yesterday was a dead man, and ordained for those under his hand mysteries and rites. [15]

14.14.2.en: The author gives an example of the origin of idol worship. A father who lost his young son made a statue for him as a memorial, and the remembrance turned into worship, and he devised for himself a particular system for worshipping the statue of his son.

14.14.3.en: It is natural that children and grandchildren should worship their ancestors (2 Macc 11:13), but the worship of dead children was also known among the Egyptians and others.

14.14.4.en: It is reported of Cicero the famous orator that he deified his daughter Tullia after her death.

14.15.0.en: Then this wicked custom became firmly established with the passing of time, and was kept as a law, and by the commands of kings the carved images became objects of worship. [16]

14.15.1.en: The second example of the origin of idolatry is the kings' setting up statues to honor themselves, and then demanding that the people worship them.

14.15.2.en: The deification of rulers was spread by Euhemerus about 290 B.C.

14.16.0.en: And men who could not honor them in their presence, because of the distance of their dwelling, portrayed their likeness from afar, and made a visible image of the king whom they honored, that by their zeal they might express flattery to the absent as though present. [17]

14.16.1.en: Among the chief evils of idol worship is the instilling of the spirit of hypocrisy, for the great and the people vied with one another to offer worship to the statues of kings out of flattery and adulation, regarding his statue as standing in his place.

14.16.2.en: * Let us reckon that all idol worship is worship offered to men...

14.16.3.en: Idol worship is condemned not because of the persons who are the object of worship, but because of its being practiced on behalf of demons. “Render therefore unto Caesar the things which are Caesar's” (Mt 22:21; Mk 12:17; Lk 20:25).

14.16.4.en: It is enough to set against this: “Render unto God the things that are God's.” What then remains for Caesar...? The Lord asked that they bring Him money, and asked whose image is this? And when He heard that it was Caesar's, He said: “Render therefore unto Caesar the things which are Caesar's.”

14.16.5.en: * We pray to the eternal God, the true God, the living God, for the health of our rulers...

14.16.6.en: It is fitting for them to realize from whom they received their authority, that as men they know from whom they received life itself. They are convinced that He is the only God, and on His power they depend entirely...

14.16.7.en: To Him we Christians lift up our eyes and spread out our hands, being innocent, and with our heads uncovered because we have no need to be ashamed, and finally without anyone to prompt us, because we pray from the heart, and pray constantly for all our emperors. We ask for them a long life, a peaceful empire, a safe dwelling, strong armies, a faithful senate, a world at peace, and everything that this man and Caesar desire.

14.16.8.en: * We honor the Emperor as we are permitted to honor him, as a man who comes after God.

14.17.0.en: 18 Also the singular diligence of the artificer helped to set forward the ignorant to more superstition. 19 For he, perhaps willing to please one in authority, labored with all his skill to make the likeness of the best fashion. 20 And so the multitude, allured by the grace of the work, took him now for a god, who a little before was but honored as a man. 21 And this was an occasion to deceive the world: for men, serving either calamity or tyranny, ascribed unto stones and stocks the incommunicable Name.

14.17.1.en: Then the ambition of the artist impelled even those who did not know him to spread his worship. [18]

14.17.2.en: Misuse of gifts: the artist who makes statues does not make them for kings as they are, but they labor to pour upon them a touch of beauty that is not found in the kings themselves. So art was turned into a snare to catch men into evil.

14.18.0.en: And perhaps he wished to please the king, so he strained his art that the result might be more beautiful than the reality. [19]

14.18.1.en: With the skill with which the artist was endowed, what occupies him is not respect for his artistic gift but pleasing the king, for material or moral gain.

14.19.0.en: So the crowd, allured by the splendor of his work, took for a god him whom a little before they honored as a man. [20]

14.19.1.en: The artist misused his gift, and offered his art to entice men to attribute divinity to a man. And God Himself warned us of this, saying: “I am the Lord: that is My name: and My glory will I not give to another, neither My praise to graven images” (Isa 42:8).

14.20.0.en: And this became a hidden snare for mankind, that men enslaved by calamity or royal authority gave to stones and wood the incommunicable Name. [21]

14.20.1.en: The wise man counts the setting up of idols and the worship of them as a catastrophe, whose motive is often the love of power and temporal glory, so that emperors and the great set up their statues as objects of worship, to which the people give what is fitting for God alone.

14.21.0.en: 22 Afterward it was not enough for them that they erred in the knowledge of God, but they live in the great war of ignorance, and those so great plagues they call peace. 23 For while they slay their children in sacrifices, or use secret ceremonies, or make revels of strange rites; 24 they keep neither lives nor marriages any longer pure, but one slays another traitorously, or grieves him by adultery. 25 So that there reigns in all men without exception blood, manslaughter, theft and dissimulation, corruption, unfaithfulness, tumults, perjury, 26 disquieting of good men, forgetfulness of good turns, defiling of souls, changing of kind, disorder in marriages, adultery and shameless uncleanness. 27 For the worship of idols not to be named is the beginning, the cause, and the end of all evil. 28 For either they are mad when they are merry, or prophesy lies, or live unjustly, or lightly forswear themselves. 29 For insomuch as their trust is in idols, which have no life, though they swear falsely, yet they look not to be hurt.

14.21.1.en: After setting forth the motives for the worship of idols, namely fornication and the love of vainglory, the immortalizing of the dead and flattery of emperors and the great, he tells us of the role of idol worship in deceiving men.

14.22.0.en: Then it was not enough for them to err in the knowledge of God, but they plunged into the wide war of ignorance, and called such evils peace. [22]

14.22.1.en: If pagan worship puts weak creatures and lifeless, dead idols in the place of God, and offers them the worship and glorification fitting for God alone, what is more serious than this is that in doing so they deceive themselves, claiming to be in deep inner peace. For more serious than ignorance is that a man should suppose in his ignorance that he has wisdom, and in his deprivation of inner peace that he is possessed of peace.

14.22.2.en: Perhaps he means here that idol worshippers used to hold feasts and practice evils and abominations under the cover of joy and peace. The wicked look upon the children of God as though they were devoid of life, joy and peace. And they pretend to grieve for the believers because they are deprived of happiness.

14.22.3.en: The wicked theological thought of the pagans drives them to a life of licentious amusement.

14.22.4.en: * Christ is our peace (Rom 5:1). Therefore the way of peace is the way of Christ, which the wicked do not know.

14.23.0.en: We saw the wise man looking with bitterness at idol worshippers because they were ignorant of the true knowledge of God, and in this ignorance they suppose that they enjoy happiness and peace. Now he adds a third factor, namely their performing shameful practices and rites unbecoming to them as men.

14.23.1.en: And with their rites that kill children, and their hidden mysteries, or their insane festivals with strange customs. [23]

14.23.2.en: By the word “rites” he means “ceremonies”; instead of the ceremony being an order fitting for man in God's holy creation, killing became among their important ceremonies, under the cover of offering sacrifices to the gods. Fathers lost their fatherhood and mothers their motherhood, and they agreed together to offer children as sacrifices to the pagan gods.

14.23.3.en: And if they were asked what lies behind this brutal act, they answered: It is a hidden mystery that none can understand.

14.23.4.en: Besides this brutal violence they practice strange customs on the days of their festivals, which often means perverse bodily practices.

14.23.5.en: Pope Athanasius the Apostolic gives us horrible examples of human sacrifices, of which we mention: 1. Some used to offer men as sacrifices to idols bearing the image of dead men, offering living creatures as sacrifices to dead creatures, and rational beings to motionless things. 2. The Taurians, a division of the Scythians, who lived in the Crimean peninsula in southern Russia. They used to seize those who had escaped from wrecked ships and offer them as sacrifices to their virgin, as they call her. So in cruelty and brutality they show that those whom their gods saved from drowning are slaughtered. 3. Some of the Scythians used to divide the spoils of war into groups, each group comprising a hundred men, and they chose one from each group and slaughtered him as an offering to their gods. 4. The ancient Egyptians used to offer human sacrifices to Hera. The Cretans and Phoenicians used to appease the face of Cronos by slaughtering their children. Even the ancient Romans used to offer human sacrifices in their worship of Jupiter Latius, the god who was regarded as protector of the Italian league composed of thirty Latin cities.

14.24.0.en: They no longer keep purity in life, nor in marriage, but one kills another, or grieves him by adultery. [24]

14.24.1.en: When they deprive themselves of fellowship with the Holy One, they are joined to Satan, who cannot bear chastity and holiness, but wants every man to fall into defilement, even in marriage, practicing perverse and unseemly things.

14.24.2.en: Their rule becomes pleasure whatever the cost, so there is nothing to prevent a man from killing another to seize his wife or daughter. He may even rape her before his eyes, threatening him with death, and this is what he means by “grieves him by adultery.”

14.25.0.en: Evil abounds, for there is blood and killing and theft and deceit and corruption and unfaithfulness and tumult and false witness. [25]

14.25.1.en: When man leaves the worship of the living God, his life turns into a chain of evils that does not stop, “evil abounds.” He cares nothing for the shedding of blood, or killing, or theft, or deceit, or corruption, or unfaithfulness, or tumult, or false witness.

14.26.0.en: And confusion of values and ingratitude for grace, and defiling of souls, and sexual perversion, and disorder in marriage, and adultery and licentiousness. [26]

14.26.1.en: They live without any regard for human or social values, with denial of divine grace, and defilement of soul and body, and licentiousness, and so on.

14.26.2.en: Idol worshippers suppose that as free men it is their right to practice evils and perversions in unrestrained wantonness. They are rights that no one may deprive them of.

14.26.3.en: * Rachel, that is the Church or discernment, hid the idols (Gen 31:34), for the Church does not know statues and forms of idols in which there is nothing of the truth, but knows the true existence of the Trinity. Truly she destroys the darkness and declares the radiance of glory. Let us then forsake the darkness and seek the sun. Let us leave the smoke and strive for the light. Smoke is evil; for as smoke is to the eyes (Prov 10:26), so is evil to those who practice it.

14.27.0.en: St. Ambrose For the worship of nameless idols is the beginning, the cause and the end of all evil. [27]

14.27.1.en: The wise man sees that idol worship does not deserve to have a name, because it rejects the name of the Holy One, and that it is the source of all evil, and behind all corruption and dissolution and license, and indeed it is the goal of evil, in which man denies his Creator and worships the wicked enemy in one form or another.

14.28.0.en: For those who worship them rejoice to madness, or prophesy lies, or live in injustice, or lightly bear false witness. [28]

14.28.1.en: After speaking of the effect of idol worship, from the lulling of the conscience to the rejection of fellowship with the holy God, and the practice of every sort of evils, he makes clear that the wicked cover evil with an atmosphere of joy, but it is not the calm inner joy, but “they rejoice to madness”; they claim prophecy, helped in this by the devil the liar, and they walk in a spirit of injustice and false witness. This was characteristic of the priests of the idols in particular.

14.28.2.en: * The father (Jacob) was commanded to dwell there in Bethel, and there he was commanded to make an altar to God who appeared to him (Gen 35:1). There he took the strange gods and buried them under the terebinth (Gen 35:4) in Jerusalem. There also Rachel was buried on the way to Ephrath, that is Bethlehem (Gen 35:19), and there Jacob set a pillar upon her grave (Gen 35:20). What great mysteries! There is the Church of God, where God appeared and spoke with His humble servants.

14.28.3.en: There the idols of the Gentiles are taken away and buried, for the faith of the Church shatters every practice of idolatry. I ask: why did he bury them under the terebinth? Surely because it is one of the unfruitful trees; so the gods of the Gentiles are there, where there is no fruit.

14.28.4.en: St. Ambrose Perhaps some may ask: How can idols prophesy, even falsely?

14.28.5.en: Holy Scripture links idol worship with false gods or demons, and counts their priests as false priests and their prophets as false prophets, because those who serve him and are moved in all their actions by Satan are called “a liar, and the father of it.” Therefore idols are called “false gods” as “the gods of the heathen are idols (demons)” (see Ps 96:5).

14.29.0.en: For since their trust is in lifeless idols, they do not expect to be harmed when they swear falsely. [29]

14.29.1.en: As they prophesy falsely, they swear and bear false witness, for they do not fear the gods, because they are statues in which there is no spirit, and cannot harm them.

14.29.2.en: They worship them and are zealous for them, and resist him who worships the true God, but in their depths they do not believe in them.

14.29.3.en: St. Ambrose * He says: Let those whom you call gods tell you of past events or prophesy to you of future events (see Isa 44:7).

14.30.0.en: 30 Therefore shall justice overtake them for both: because they thought badly of God, giving heed unto idols, and swore unjustly, in deceit, despising holiness. 31 For it is not the power of them by whom they swear, but it is the just vengeance of sinners, that punishes always the offence of the ungodly.

14.30.1.en: There are two things for which they deserve that punishment come upon them:

14.30.2.en: Their evil thinking about God by following idols, and their deceitful oath falsely sworn, by despising holiness. [30]

14.30.3.en: Punishment comes upon idol worshippers for two things:

14.30.4.en: First: their rejection of the worship of the living God by accepting idols in His place.

14.30.5.en: Second: false swearing and contempt of holiness. Here, in speaking of the wicked life or wicked conduct, he concentrates on the lying tongue, which swears falsely, and the unclean, reckless life that cares nothing for holiness and purity and chastity.

14.31.0.en: For what always follows the transgression of the unrighteous is not the power of those by whom they swear, but the judgment upon sinners. [31]

14.31.1.en: He brings out here a point of the greatest importance, namely that though idolaters swear by false gods, false swearing is evil even if it is in the name of false gods, because lying in itself is sin whether with an oath or without it.

14.31.2.en: Arise within me, O wisdom of God,
